steps.what: Show the jam location the sorting equipment reports.
Clear the jam in the sorting equipment.
Record that the sorting equipment is running again.

tasks.design: When the sorting equipment reports a jam, {OPS_SYSTEM} shows that location. The mail sorter clears the jam by hand and records that the equipment is running again. A jam with no location code is found by the sorter. The screen does not clear the jam, and the note does not score the sorter.
tasks.previous_blocker: The sorter walked the machine to find the jam.
tasks.enabler_now: The equipment can show a jam location it has already detected.
tasks.still_hard: Paper wrapped in a roller has to be pulled out by hand.
tasks.human_edge: The sorter's hands clear the jam. A location code only shortens the search.
tasks.altitude: Clearing the jam stays with the sorter. The screen only shows a location the equipment already reported.

reach.task: Keep a delivery round moving when a bag is stuck.
reach.learn: A reported location is not the repair.

evidence.claim: Sorting equipment can display a jam location it has already detected. It cannot pull the mail out.
A restart note about the machine is not a record of how fast the sorter worked.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A mail sorter on the floor of a mid-size European organisation. A code on a screen does not pick up, sort, or rewrap a piece of mail.
Fields: An equipment id is required before a location is shown. With no code, the sorter searches the machine. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the mail sorter finishes it by hand.
Native check: The note names the equipment and the time. It does not name a performance score.
The note is about the item or the machine. It is not a score of the sorter.
unknowns: Whether this equipment reports a jam code or only stops.
research_questions: Which jams are found only by walking the machine?

already_counted.description: Clearing the jam and recording the restart stay with the sorter.

incremental.description: Check the location on the screen is the machine that stopped.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes the equipment reports no jam code, so the sorter searches by hand and nothing is saved. High assumes a location is shown and the clearing itself is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the various types of computer equipment assigned to this run.
Operate scanning equipment, addressographs, mimeographs, optical character readers, and bar-code sorters.
Note a stop on the equipment the sorter was operating.

tasks.design: The various types of computer equipment assigned to the run are shown from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The mail sorter operates the scanning equipment, addressographs, mimeographs, optical character readers, and bar-code sorters. A machine with no assignment id is not listed. The list does not run the equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: The sorter learned which machine to run from a paper roster that was often stale.
tasks.enabler_now: The run record can show which equipment is assigned before the sorter starts it.
tasks.still_hard: Feeding, watching, and stopping the machine are the sorter's hands and eyes.
tasks.human_edge: The sorter operates the equipment for the whole run. An assignment list does not feed it.
tasks.altitude: Operating the equipment stays with the sorter. The screen only shows which machine the run assigned.

reach.role: Weighers, Measurers, Checkers, and Samplers, Recordkeeping
reach.task: Run a scale or a meter for a shift.
reach.learn: An assignment is not the operation.

evidence.claim: A run record can list equipment already assigned. It cannot feed a scanner or a bar-code sorter.
A stop note is about the machine. It is not an evaluation of the sorter.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A mail sorter on the floor of a mid-size European organisation. A code on a screen does not pick up, sort, or rewrap a piece of mail.
Fields: A run id and an equipment id are required. A machine with no assignment is not listed. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the mail sorter finishes it by hand.
Native check: The sorter starts, feeds, and stops the equipment. The list does not.
The note is about the item or the machine. It is not a score of the sorter.
unknowns: Which of these machine types this floor still uses.
research_questions: Which runs are still assigned on paper rather than on the equipment record?

already_counted.description: Operating the equipment and noting a stop stay with the sorter.

incremental.description: Check the listed machine is the one at this station.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes the run has no equipment ids, so the sorter finds the machine as today. High assumes the assignment is on screen. Operating the machine is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the special handling bins for this shift.
Sort odd-sized items other workers were unable to sort.

tasks.design: Special handling bins for the shift are shown from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The mail sorter sorts odd-sized items by hand, including mail other workers were unable to sort, and segregates items that require special handling. A bin with no id is not shown. The screen does not sort the piece.
tasks.previous_blocker: Special bins were known by habit, so a new sorter guessed.
tasks.enabler_now: The shift record can show which bin is for which kind of special handling.
tasks.still_hard: An odd shape still has to be looked at and placed by hand.
tasks.human_edge: The sorter decides the piece and places it. The bin list does not.
tasks.altitude: Hand sorting stays with the sorter. The screen only names the bins.

reach.task: Separate an item that will not go in the usual bag.
reach.learn: A bin name is not the sort.

evidence.claim: A shift record can name the special-handling bins. It cannot judge an odd-sized piece.
Hand sorting of mail that a machine could not place stays with the sorter.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A mail sorter on the floor of a mid-size European organisation. A code on a screen does not pick up, sort, or rewrap a piece of mail.
Fields: A shift id and a bin id are required. With no bin id, the sorter uses the bins they already know. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the mail sorter finishes it by hand.
Native check: Every odd-sized piece is placed by hand. Nothing is auto-sorted in this task.
unknowns: Whether special-handling categories are stable across shifts.
research_questions: Which odd-sized pieces have no bin and are still decided on the spot?

already_counted.description: Sorting by hand and segregating special items stay with the sorter.

incremental.description: Check the bin list matches this shift's special handling.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes the shift has no bin ids, so nothing is shown and the hand sort is unchanged. High assumes the bins are named. The sort itself stays by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct items by the routing scheme.

steps.what: Load the established routing schemes for this run.
Direct items according to those schemes, using computer-controlled keyboards or voice-recognition equipment.
Set aside items the routing scheme does not place.

tasks.design: The established routing scheme for the run is loaded in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The mail sorter directs each item according to that scheme, using computer-controlled keyboards or voice-recognition equipment. An item the scheme does not place is set aside. The loaded scheme does not key the item.
tasks.previous_blocker: The scheme sat on a printed card, and a change was easy to miss.
tasks.enabler_now: The current scheme can be loaded before the sorter starts keying.
tasks.still_hard: Reading the item and keying or speaking the route is the sorter's work.
tasks.human_edge: The sorter directs the item. A loaded scheme is the rule, not the keystroke.
tasks.altitude: The sorter still directs each item. Loading the scheme only removes the hunt for the current card.

reach.task: Follow the route they are given.
reach.learn: A scheme is the rule. Someone still applies it to the item.

evidence.claim: An established routing scheme can be loaded onto the station. The sorter still keys or speaks each item.
An item the scheme does not recognise stays with the sorter. The load does not invent a route.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A mail sorter on the floor of a mid-size European organisation. A code on a screen does not pick up, sort, or rewrap a piece of mail.
Fields: A scheme id is required. With no scheme id, the sorter uses the card they already have. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the mail sorter finishes it by hand.
Native check: The sorter directs the item. The equipment does not take that keystroke away in this task.
unknowns: Whether voice recognition on this floor is in use or only keyboards.
research_questions: Which items are still set aside because the scheme has no route for them?

already_counted.description: Directing each item and setting aside the unplaced ones stay with the sorter.

incremental.description: Check the loaded scheme is the one for this run.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes there is no scheme id, so the sorter works from the printed card. High assumes the current scheme is loaded. Keying or speaking each item is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The mail sorter still clears the jam, still runs the scanning equipment, and still sorts odd-sized mail by hand. A screen can show a jam location or a routing scheme the equipment already holds. It does not touch the mail.
reach: Postal service mail carriers receive bundles that are already routed, and this job learns the routing scheme does not pick up the item.
Postal service clerks face the public counter, and this job learns the floor work is the piece of mail, not a form.
skills_to_grow: Clear a jam from the location the equipment reports, and find it by hand when there is no code.
Run the scanner or the bar-code sorter for the whole run, including the stops.
Sort by hand anything the scheme does not place.
role.ambitious_version: Each run starts with the scheme and the jam codes the equipment already has, and every piece the scheme cannot place is still sorted by the sorter's hands.
